_about: concepts.<c>.keys: string resources whose English text expresses concept <c>. For every locale that has a
locales.<l>.terms.<c> entry, each keyed string must contain at least one 'allowed' stem and no 'forbidden' stem.
Matching: NFC-normalized, lower-cased with Locale.ROOT, U+0307 (combining dot) dropped. A stem must start a
word (preceded by start-of-text or a non-letter/non-mark character) unless the locale sets matchAnywhere
(compounding languages and scripts written without spaces).
Stems were chosen from the DOMINANT established usage in each strings.xml (counts recorded in 'note') and,
where usage was genuinely split, from AOSP LatinIME's translation (see docs/i18n/2026-09-29-terminology.md).
Machine-derived: no entry here is native-speaker reviewed.

locales.<l>.register: the address register (formal/informal/neutral) and Java regexes for forms of the OTHER register; no string or plural item in that locale may match. Enforced by TranslationGlossaryTest.everyStringUsesTheLocalesAddressRegister; decisions in docs/i18n/2026-09-29-register.md.

Sie-register throughout: 33 strings with mid-sentence 'Sie', 21 with 'Ihr/Ihre/Ihren'; imperatives are either 'Tippen Sie …' or the impersonal infinitive ('Zum Umordnen ziehen'). AOSP LatinIME de uses du ('deinem', 'kannst', 'Aktiviere'), i.e. it DISAGREES, but AOSP is only a tie-breaker and the file is not tied (43:0). Pattern 3 (du-imperative + object) matched nothing before either, so all three patterns are diagnostic guards.

register.note: vous-register: 'vous' 14, 'votre/vos' 25, -ez imperatives 40+ ('Appuyez' 7, 'Saisissez' 7, 'Importez' 4, 'Touchez' 3 …). No tu/ton/ta/tes/2sg forms. The 4 counter hits were 3sg descriptions ('Utilise des expressions courantes' = 'uses', 'Copie le texte' = 'copies') and the shell flag '--es'; -er-verb tu-imperatives are morphologically identical to 3sg, so pattern 3 only fires with an instruction-shaped complement (sur/ici/deux fois/…), never with a plain noun object. 'ton' is included although it can also mean 'tone' (0 occurrences today). AOSP fr: vous ('Appuyez', 'votre'). All patterns are guards (0 pre-existing hits).

Ön-register: explicit 'Ön' 4, 3sg-imperative (Ön) forms 'Koppintson' 7, 'Húzza' 3, 'Hagyja' 3, 'Adja/Adjon' 4, 'Próbálja' 2, 'Kapcsolja' 2, 'Érintse' 2, 'Válasszon', 'Állítsa', 'Gépeljen', 'Csúsztasson', 'Rendelje', 'Töltse', 'Használja', 'Írjon' … (45 strings) plus '-hatja/-heti' potentials; te-register only in 2 strings: privacy_section_intro ('eszközödet', 'megnézhesd', 'exportálhasd', 'törölhesd') and privacy_delete_data_body ('törlöd'). Suffix scans over every word (-sz/-od/-ed/-öd/-d/-j/-hasd/-hesd) found no other 2sg form ('vagy' = or, 'kell' = impersonal must, 'majd', 'mind' are not verbs). AOSP hu: Ön ('Koppintson', 'Írjon', 'Állítson', 'Ön'). Both strings corrected (eszközét / megnézhesse, exportálhassa, törölhesse / törli). Pattern 2 and 4 matched the two strings before; 1 and 3 are guards.

Anda-register (Indonesian UI standard): 'Anda' in 29 strings, capitalised; zero kamu/-mu/kau. Pattern 2 catches the enclitic possessive -mu ('perangkatmu') with the common non-pronoun -mu words excluded; slang lo/lu/gue are not included because 'Lo-Fi'-style tokens would false-positive. AOSP in: Anda (11). Both guards.

register.note: tu-register: 2sg imperatives dominate (Tocca 7 sentence-initial, Abilita 13, Usa 8, Seleziona 8, Aggiungi 8, Inserisci 7 …), 'tuo/tua' 6, 'puoi/hai/vuoi' 8, 'tu' 1: 100 strings with tu-markers vs 0 Lei-imperatives. The 33 'formal' counter hits are articles at sentence start ('La password…', 'Le importazioni…') and 3sg descriptions ('può', 'ha', 'deve'). 'Lei/Suo/Sua' cannot be forbidden case-insensitively (lei = she, suo = its: 'delle sue parole' refers to the language pack), so the guard is the Lei-imperative list with an instruction-shaped complement ('attivi'/'usi' are excluded as adjective/noun collisions) plus courtesy formulas. AOSP it: tu ('Tocca', 'tuo', 'Vuoi'). Both patterns are guards.

register.note: です/ます (polite) for every sentence: 'ます。' 87, 'ません。' 29, 'ください。' 18, 'です。' 16, 'ました' 11 (186 strings); dictionary-form labels ('設定を開く') are the normal neutral label style and are not sentences. The counter's 19 'plain' hits were the last kana of 'ください。' and 'でした。' (pattern refined with lookbehinds). 'あなた' (1 string) is acceptable polite usage; 君/お前 are the informal pronouns and are guarded. AOSP ja: です/ます ('ます' 33, 'ください' 5). Both patterns are guards.

Polite (존댓말) throughout: sentence-final -습니다/-합니다/-됩니다 (150+), -세요 (28), -입니다 (12); no 반말 (-한다/-해/-야) and no 너. The counter's 24 'informal' hits were nouns ending in 자/어/지 (관리자, 언어, 페이지, 감지, 메시지) and '%1$d자'. Both 합쇼체 and 해요체 are polite, so mixing them is not a T/V error and is not flagged. AOSP ko: same (-습니다 15, -합니다 9, -세요 6). All three patterns are guards.

Brazilian você-register (3sg forms): 'você' 12, 'seu/sua/seus/suas' 23, 3sg imperatives 'Toque' 13, 'Digite' 5, 'Arraste' 4, 'Ajuste' 3, 'pode' 12, 'precisa' 4; zero tu/teu/2sg-'-s' forms (the single counter hit 'Copia o texto' is a 3sg description). Vocabulary is pt-BR (senha 21, tela 10, arquivo 15, aplicativo 6, salvar 3) with a few pt-PT leaks ('arranque', 'predefinido', 'guardar' 1) that are terminology, not register. 'Formal' here means the você/3sg form; pt-BR has no separate polite form in UI. Imperatives cannot be used as markers (tu-imperative = 3sg indicative for -ar/-er/-ir verbs, e.g. 'Copia', 'adiciona' appear as descriptions), so only pronouns/possessives/2sg verb endings are forbidden. register.note: Formal (dumneavoastră) register decided on unambiguous markers: 'dvs.' 13 strings, 'vă/dumneavoastră' 3, 'puteți/veți/doriți' 5, 2pl instruction imperatives ~45 ('Ștergeți' 7, 'Introduceți' 6, 'Atingeți' 5, 'Importați' 4, 'Folosiți' 5, 'Tastați' 5, 'Lăsați' 2 …, plus 'în timp ce scrieți/glisați/tastați') versus 2sg-only markers in 11 strings ('tastatura ta' 2, 'a-ți/-ți' 2, 'vrei să ștergi', 'să setezi', 'Vezi' 2, 'Elimini', 'glisezi', 'afișezi', 'limitezi') and 2sg instruction imperatives in ~15 ('Atinge pentru…' 9, 'Trage pentru' 4, 'Atinge aici', 'Dezactivează pentru', 'Lasă valoarea'). AOSP ro is formal everywhere ('Atingeți', 'Ștergeți', 'Anulați', 'dvs.'). Short command labels and setting summaries use the -ă/-ează form ('Adaugă', 'Șterge', 'Afișează 13', 'Activează 12'), which is morphologically identical to the 3sg indicative and is the file's label convention; those ~150 strings were NOT changed and are not matched by the patterns (pattern 3 only fires with an instruction-shaped complement). 26 strings (28 items incl. the layout_manager_hint plural) corrected to -ți forms / 'dvs.' / 'vă'. Pattern 4 is the generic 2sg '-ezi' ending (no Romanian noun in the file ends in -ezi). Patterns 1-4 matched 4, 6, 18 and 4 strings before the corrections.

вы-register: 2pl imperatives in 80 strings ('Введите' 8, 'Нажмите' 5, 'Выберите' 5, 'Перетащите' 5, 'Импортируйте' 4, 'Коснитесь' …), 'ваш/ваше/вами', 'можете'; zero ты/твой/-ешь/-ишь. Pattern 2 is the generic 2sg verb ending with 'лишь' excluded (the only common non-verb in -ишь); 'настрой' and 'удали' were dropped from the imperative list (noun 'настрой', past-tense reading). AOSP ru: вы ('Выберите', 'нажмите', 'можете'). All patterns are guards.

Bare-stem imperatives in titles, buttons and setting summaries ('Sil', 'Tema Oluştur', 'Kaydırma İzini Etkinleştir', 'Klavyede GIF tuşunu göster', 'İmleci sola taşı') are the standard Turkish UI convention (AOSP tr: 'Hareket izini göster', 'Bölünmüş klavyeyi etkinleştir', but 'Kaydetmek için tekrar dokunun') and do not mark the T-register; they are untouched. The '-sin' words in the file are 3sg optatives ('silinsin', 'unutulsun'), not 2sg. One outlier corrected: gesture_double_space_period_desc 'boşluğa iki kez hızlıca dokun.' → 'dokunun.'. Pattern 4 catches an 'için …'-clause instruction that ends in a lowercase bare imperative plus a full stop (the '(?-i:…)' group is deliberately case-sensitive so Title-Case labels like 'Caps Lock için Shift'e Çift Dokun' are not flagged); it matched that one string before. Patterns 1-3 are guards.

register.note: 你 dominates: 25 occurrences in 21 strings vs 您 in 4 strings (short_swipe_instruction_body, theme_decorative_desc, test_keyboard_hint, clipboard_custom_rules_desc — the same 'batch' of strings that carries the odd register in ro/hu).
